messages:
sara_support: Customer on Dedicated reported a sudden spike of 403s after an IdP key rotation. They say requests hit the LB but the backend sees no Authorization header. repro steps attached.

kevin_sre: Can you paste the exact curl they used? Also which deployment mode (VPC public LB / private)?

sara_support: Dedicated, private VPC edge (internal ALB -> haproxy TCP -> istio ingress). Their curl (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' https://dedicated.example.customer/v1/generate
```
Response: 403 with body "missing credentials" from our auth middleware. LB logs show 200 to haproxy, then 403 from service.

ashley_platform: Interesting. ALB might be terminating TLS and doing some authn mapping. Does the ALB have "preserve host header" or any header rewrite rule?

juan_infra: Also check haproxy config. If it's in TCP mode with PROXY protocol and then passing to istio, some setups accidentally route to the wrong listener and Envoy strips inbound auth headers when doing mTLS origination.

sara_support: Customer says they didn't change haproxy. They rotated IdP signing keys yesterday. Works for hosted customers, only affected Dedicated. They attached a gateway trace:
```
[edge] ALB -> haproxy (tcp) -> istio-ingress -> internal-gw -> service
headers at edge: Authorization: Bearer XXX, Cookie: session=YYY
headers at service: Cookie: session=YYY  (no Authorization)
```

kevin_sre: That pattern screams "header suppressed by Envoy/ISTIO when mTLS origination on the ingress gateway". If the istio ingress is performing external auth (ext_authz) or JWT filter, misconfiguration can strip the header after validation when the peer identity doesn't match.

ashley_platform: Another angle: are they using token-binding via cookies? Some on-prem IdP setups use a cookie that is exchanged at the edge and then the gateway sets an X-Forwarded-Authorization or transforms the cookie into a short-lived Authorization header. If that transformation fails post-rotation, the header may not be added.

juan_infra: Request we get: haproxy config (frontend/backend), istio ingress config (Gateway, VirtualService, ext_authz plugin config), and a tcpdump of the traffic between istio and internal-gw (sanitized).

sara_support: Shared minimal repro from customer attached. Quick grep of istio filters shows ext_authz configured with "shadow" off and header_to_check: "authorization". They also have bearer token introspection pointing to an internal introspector that recently updated certs.

kevin_sre: Action plan:
1) Ask customer to test with a simple direct request to internal service bypassing ingress (if possible) to confirm service accepts Authorization.
2) Turn on debug logs for istio ext_authz plugin to see if header is present on arrival and if plugin returns DENY or OK.
3) If ext_authz returns OK but header disappears, check envoy header_operations—there may be a "remove" rule after authn.

ashley_platform: Also check if haproxy is using http/2 to edge and then HTTP/1.1 upstream; header name casing and fragmentation sometimes cause proxy to drop long headers. But Authorization is short, so less likely.

sara_support: Customer tried direct call to internal service -> internal service accepted the same bearer token. So token itself is valid and introspection works. The header is reliably absent once traffic crosses istio ingress.

juan_infra: Confirmed hypothesis: ext_authz configured to call introspector with mTLS. When the IdP rotated keys, the introspector started rejecting token introspection calls due to failing client cert validation. Envoy then responded with 401 to the client but because of how the filter chain was set, Authorization header was removed from the forwarded request (envoy behavior).

kevin_sre: Workaround options while we fix introspector certs:
- Toggle ext_authz to respond "failed open" (shadow mode) temporarily so it doesn't remove headers.
- Configure envoy to forward original headers even on auth failure (header_operations to add "authorization" back from x-forwarded-auth if present).

ashley_platform: Recommended fix: rotate the client cert used by introspector to a valid cert trusted by istio, and/or relax TLS validation briefly. Also add a canary rule to ensure header preservation.

sara_support: I proposed a temporary canary: update their istio FilterChain to set ext_authz -> failure_mode_allow and enable detailed ext_authz logs. Customer applied failure_mode_allow and 5m later calls started succeeding. They then rolled through cert rotation with the introspector and reverted failure_mode_allow.

kevin_sre: Please create a postmortem note for the Dedicated onboarding docs: default ext_authz setup should include a fallback-preserve-headers option and a troubleshooting checklist for IdP key rotations (check introspector certs, ext_authz logs, header_operations).

sara_support: Will open a support ticket with the remediation steps we validated and add the postmortem doc. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
